newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria bourse lists international debt fund.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria bourse lists international debt fund.

text.p: LAGOS, April 7 (Reuter) An instrument to trade Nigeria's internationally quoted debt locally was listed on the Nigerian stock market on Monday, the promoters said.
The Nigerian International Debt Fund aims to trade up to $100 million in several tranches.
It was listed under the investment companies sector of the Nigerian stock exchange.

"The issue was successful as the minimum of $10 million which was required to commence operations was exceeded," Andrew Obaseki, chief executive officer of fund manager Securities Transactions and Trust Company (SecTrust), said in a statement.
He said $10.57 million was raised from the issue which opened on February 17. The subscription level was put at 66.7 percent.
Obaseki said the issue was not fully subscribed because many investors made late entries.
"Many investors were calling to take up units later but we did not accept anything after the closing date of March 14," he said.
He said foreign investors, mainly Nigerian citizens based in the United States and Europe, also showed interest in the offer.
"We have been very pleased with the level of enthusiasm and interest both locally and internationally," Obaseki said on Monday.
Initial investors bought units worth at least $5,000 but trading on the secondary market will be in units of $1,000.
"With the listing it will now be possible for small investors who could not afford the minimum 50 investment notes during the primary issue to buy and sell in lots of 10 notes," Obaseki said.
He said from current development in the international markets, the investment was poised to exceed its forecast performance.
When it was floated in February, the promoters said they expected a yield of not less than eight percent, which they said was higher than U.S. money market rates.

The fund was developed last year with the involvement of the local subsidiary of America's Citibank, Nigerian International Bank (NIB) and one of Nigeria's top three banks United Bank for Africa (UBA).
A U.K.-based company Afrinvest Securities Ltd. served as an adviser to the issue.
